pages.title: Control Plane Worker
pages.purpose: The Cloudflare Worker shell: API router and route groups, authentication edges, D1 store layer, background tasks, crons and queues.
instructions: Cover the cron/queue side work: scheduler tick (recovery sweep + overdue automations), image-builds/scheduler.ts, session/abandoned-draft-sweep.ts, autofix handler + queue-health, image-build finalization consumer; note BackgroundTasks (platform-ports.ts, cloudflare/background-tasks.ts) as the ctx.waitUntil seam.

Describe the routing framework in src/routes/shared.ts (defineRoute/defineRoutes, auth variants, supportedScmProviders gating that returns 501 for unimplemented providers, CORS + x-request-id/x-trace-id headers, HttpError shape) and inventory the route groups registered in router.ts.
Explain the D1 store layer in src/db/ (one store file per aggregate, SqlDatabase port, instrumented-d1 request metrics) and the rule that env.DB is read exactly once per composition root.

Map the auth edges: user auth (auth/authenticate.ts + auth/user/ runtime, admission policy), worker-to-worker service auth via @open-inspect/shared/service-auth.ts, sandbox auth tokens, WebSocket tokens, and webhook signature verification (auth/webhook-key.ts).
Mention src/types.ts Env bindings (SESSION DO, DB, REPOS_CACHE KV, MEDIA_BUCKET R2, queues, service auth secrets) and that production bindings are Terraform-managed (wrangler.jsonc is test-only).

pages.title: Data Model & Storage
pages.purpose: Where state lives: the D1 shared schema (migrations), the per-session DO SQLite schema, key stores, and token/secret encryption.
instructions: Describe migrations: terraform/d1/migrations applied by scripts/d1-migrate.sh; control-plane integration tests apply them automatically (test/integration/apply-migrations.ts) — new tables need both a migration and store updates.

Document encryption at rest: AES-256-GCM (auth/crypto.ts) for participant GitHub tokens, scoped-secrets.ts for global/repo/environment secrets, provider-account-crypto.ts + model-provider-account-atomic-writer.ts for managed credentials; secrets-validation.ts enforces key rules.

Embed a mermaid erDiagram for the core entities (Session, SessionRepository, Environment, Automation, AutomationInvocation, AutomationRun, ImageBuild, Skill) per the mermaid-diagrams skill; keep entity names identifier-like.

Enumerate the important D1 tables using packages/control-plane/README.md's D1 schema section plus terraform/d1/migrations: session_repositories (position 0 = primary; scalar mirror on the session row), environments/environment_repositories/environment_secrets, image_builds unified registry (scope_kind/scope_id, repository_shas fingerprint, runtime version floor, queue-lease state), automations/automation_repositories/automation_environments/automation_invocations (trigger_key dedupe, derived status SQL in automation-store.ts)/automation_runs (firing-time repo snapshot), skills + skill_profiles, integration_settings three-layer tables, model provider account tables, user_store + user_scm_tokens.

Frame the two storage layers: shared D1 (cross-session: sessions index, environments, automations, image builds, secrets, skills, users, model-provider accounts) and per-session DO-embedded SQLite (hot session state); SQL access goes through db/sql-database.ts with per-aggregate stores in db/.

pages.title: Sandbox Providers & Infra
pages.purpose: The SandboxProvider abstraction, the five provider implementations and their REST clients, the lifecycle manager's decision layer, and the provider infra packages.
instructions: Cover the infra packages: modal-infra (web_api.py endpoints authenticated via verify_internal_token, sandbox/manager.py, sandbox/build_session.py, images/base.py with CACHE_BUSTER), daytona-infra bootstrap, e2b-infra template Dockerfile, opencomputer-infra build-template.ts.

Explain sandbox/lifecycle/manager.ts orchestration: pure decision functions in lifecycle/decisions.ts (spawn, warm, inactivity, heartbeat health, connecting timeout, circuit breaker with spawn_failure_count) executed through injected SandboxStorage/SessionContextReader ports; image-selection.ts picks prebuilt images at spawn.

Give a provider matrix: Modal (client.ts → packages/modal-infra web_api with HMAC internal tokens, snapshot restore), Daytona (daytona-rest-client.ts, persistent stop/start), Vercel (providers/vercel/ with base-snapshot bootstrap), OpenComputer (opencomputer-rest-client.ts, template/checkpoint builds), E2B (e2b-rest-client.ts, pause/resume). Note which support prebuilt-image builds (Modal, Vercel, OpenComputer).
Mention request-deadline.ts timeouts and that sandbox auth tokens are minted (JWT) by the control plane per sandbox.

Start from sandbox/provider.ts: the SandboxProvider interface, SandboxProviderCapabilities (supportsSnapshots, supportsRestore, supportsPersistentResume, supportsExplicitStop), CreateSandboxConfig, and ImageBuildProviderTriggerConfig; provider-factory.ts selects the provider from env and throws on missing credentials.

pages.title: Sandbox Runtime (Data Plane)
pages.purpose: The Python in-sandbox runtime package: supervisor composition, agent bridge to the control plane, OpenCode server, repository boot/hooks/sync, credential helper, agent tools, and image-build mode.
instructions: Conventions that matter here: Python timeouts in seconds; repo owners may contain '/' (repo_config.py is_safe_repo_owner — only repo_name is a single path segment).

Cover bridge.py: the WebSocket client to the control plane DO (heartbeat, reconnection, acks, buffered event forwarding via event_forwarder.py, prompt streaming via prompt_stream.py, git identity per prompt via message_attribution.py, diff capture via diff_capture/diff_collector.py, push command handling).
Document credentials: credentials/git_credential_helper.py brokers short-lived SCM tokens from the control plane (auth/github_app.py, auth/internal.py for HMAC tokens).

Explain boot modes via OPENINSPECT_BOOT_MODE (build, fresh, repo_image, snapshot_restore) and the .openinspect/setup.sh vs start.sh semantics from README: setup skipped on image/restore starts, start.sh strict-fail, SETUP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS/START_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, tunnel URLs written to /workspace/.tunnels.env with TUNNEL_WAIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS wait.

List the agent tools in tools/ (spawn-child, send-child-prompt, get-child-status, cancel-child, slack-notify as JS scripts) and managed_skills.py materializing pinned skills into the OpenCode global config dir.

entrypoint.py is the CLI/composition root: RuntimeConfig.from_env → SandboxSupervisor(RepositoryBoot, OpenCodeServer, AgentBridgeProcess, CodeServer, WebTerminal, BrowserDesktop, ManagedSkillsMaterializer, TunnelEnvironment); the --modal-image-build-mode argument routes to the image-build startup path.

pages.title: Session Durable Object Internals
pages.purpose: Inside SessionDO: the composition root in session/components.ts, the per-session SQLite schema, the message queue, WebSocket hub, event stream, alarms, and internal HTTP handlers.
instructions: Document the per-session SQLite schema from session/schema.ts (session, participants, messages, events, artifacts, sandbox, ws_client_mapping, session attachments) and the repository classes that own each table.

Embed a mermaid flowchart of message/event routing through the DO (per the mermaid-diagrams skill): client ws + sandbox ws → message router/queue → sandbox → event processor → repositories + broadcast.

Explain the split: durable-object.ts is a thin Cloudflare adapter (fetch, webSocketMessage/Close/Error, alarm) while session/components.ts is the composition root that builds the whole collaborator graph eagerly and throws on misconfigured deployments (sandbox provider or SCM provider errors fail every request at init, before state is written).
Note the message router / disconnect handler path and that lifecycle states are persisted before closing sockets so reconnects can't resurrect a stopped sandbox.

Trace the internals: message-queue.ts (prompt enqueue/stop semantics, queued prompts, attachments), websocket-manager.ts (client + sandbox sockets with hibernation recovery), event-stream.ts/event-repository.ts (cursors and replay), sandbox-events/processor.ts + handlers (execution/streaming/artifact/runtime events), alarm/ (persisted deadlines via PersistedAlarmDeadlineStore), http/routes.ts + handlers (internal session API), pull-request-service.ts, scm-credentials-service.ts, callback-notification-service.ts, presence/participant services, diffs/ store.

pages.title: System Overview
pages.purpose: The three-tier architecture (clients → Cloudflare control plane → sandbox data plane), the package graph, worker entrypoints, and the WebSocket spine that connects them.
instructions: Cover the worker entrypoints in packages/control-plane/src/index.ts: fetch (API router + WebSocket upgrade at /sessions/:id/ws), scheduled (three crons: image-build scheduler, abandoned-draft sweep, and the '* * * * *' tick running the automation Scheduler plus autofix queue health), and queue (autofix envelopes vs image-build finalization, routed via src/queue-routing.ts).
Embed a mermaid flowchart of the tiers/packages (per the mermaid-diagrams skill); keep labels short and follow the skill's syntax safety rules.

Explain the three tiers: clients (web, Slack, GitHub, Linear, webhooks) → control plane (Cloudflare Workers, per-session Durable Objects with embedded SQLite, shared D1, KV, R2, Queues) → data plane sandboxes (Modal/Daytona/Vercel/OpenComputer/E2B running the Python sandbox runtime with OpenCode).
Include the package dependency graph from AGENTS.md (@open-inspect/shared ← all TS packages; Python packages independent) and which package owns which runtime concern.
State the client-agnostic invariant: state lives in the control plane, so any client that can POST and open a WebSocket sees the same session.

pages.title: Web Client (Next.js)
pages.purpose: The Next.js web client: App Router structure, API proxy layer, auth session, the session-socket state reducer, realtime hooks, and major UI subsystems.
instructions: Cover auth flow: middleware.ts, auth-session/server-auth-session boundary, sign-in providers surfaced from the control plane; deployment can be Vercel or Cloudflare via OpenNext (wrangler.toml, open-next.config.ts).

Explain the realtime client: lib/session-socket/reducer.ts folds ServerMessages into view state, event-log.ts + swr-revalidation.ts handle history hydration, hooks/use-session-socket.ts and use-session-transport.ts manage the connection; warm draft sessions (use-warm-draft-session.ts) trigger proactive sandbox warming while typing.

Highlight key UI subsystems with their state sources: virtualized session timeline (session-timeline.tsx + lib/timeline-virtual-rows.ts), queued prompt stack, model/reasoning selector, session changes/diffs panel, media lightbox.

Map the App Router: (app)/(sidebar)/page.tsx dashboard, session/[id] live session view, settings pages, automations UI (components/automations), login/access-denied routes; the /api/* route handlers proxy to the control plane (browser-auth-proxy.ts, control-plane-json-proxy.ts, settings-proxy.ts, provider-account-proxy.ts).
Note the client→server message types the UI relies on (ping/subscribe/prompt/stop/typing/presence) from packages/control-plane/README.md and shared/src/types/server-messages.ts.

pages.title: Security & Tokens
pages.purpose: The security model: single-tenant trust assumptions, the four-token architecture, GitHub App brokering, service auth between workers, admission/identity enforcement, and commit signing.
instructions: Cover the credential plumbing: auth/github-app.ts (PKCS#8 private key, installation token minting), source-control/github-credential-authority.ts, and the requirement that each SCM provider implements generateCredentialHelperAuth (source-control/providers/).

Document the four token types and their scopes: GitHub App installation tokens (git clone/fetch/push, minted server-side and brokered via POST /sessions/:id/scm-credentials), user OAuth tokens (PR creation + identity), sandbox auth tokens (sandbox→control-plane calls), WebSocket tokens (per session).

Explain service-to-service auth: shared/service-auth.ts HMAC tokens between control plane and bots, callback signing (auth/service/callback-signing.ts), webhook signature verification (auth/webhook-key.ts, github-bot/verify.ts), and identity enforcement + user merge (auth/identity-enforcement.ts, db/user-merge.ts).

Include commit attribution and signing: resolveGitAuthorIdentity (session/identity.ts), attributed-user vs agent-only gitIdentity modes parsed in bridge.py, and SSH-based commit signing (auth/sshsig.ts, routes/commit-signing.ts, sandbox-runtime git_signing.py).

State the single-tenant trust model from README (all users share one GitHub App installation; no per-user repo validation at session creation) and the deployment hardening recommendations (SSO/VPN, repo-scoped App installation, ALLOWED_GITHUB_ORGS / email-domain admission via auth/user/admission-policy.ts).

pages.title: Sessions & Environments (Concepts)
pages.purpose: Domain vocabulary: session targets (single/multi-repo/environment/none), the primary-repository rule, environments, settings resolution, and snapshot vs prebuilt image concepts.
instructions: Define snapshots vs prebuilt images (restore workspace state after prompts / built-ahead clones+deps rebuilt every 30 minutes) and the session data inventory (messages, events, artifacts, participants, sandbox state) from HOW_IT_WORKS.

Environments: ordered repository list with per-repo base branches, environment-scoped secrets (repo secrets do NOT flow in), prebuild flag, Slack channel associations, integration-setting overrides; sessions launched from an environment record environmentId as provenance only.

Explain the integration-settings resolution chain (global defaults → primary-repo overrides → environment overrides) from session/integration-settings-resolution.ts and db/integration-settings.ts, and which session-scoped integrations accept which layers (sandbox, code-server).
Record invariants a coder must not break: first repository is primary; repo_owner can be a nested namespace; editing/deleting an environment never mutates existing sessions.

Session targets (from HOW_IT_WORKS + session/initialize.ts): a single repository (scalar repoOwner/repoName mirrored on the row), an ad-hoc repositories list (up to 10, position 0 is primary and drives defaults), an environment, or none; the members are snapshotted into the session at creation and never change with the source environment.

pages.title: GitHub Bot Integration
pages.purpose: The GitHub bot worker: PR auto-review and @mention handling, session targeting with default environments, and the autofix ingress into the control-plane queue.
instructions: Cover config and tests: per-repo enablement via integration settings, GitHub App auth (github-auth.ts), test layout in test/*.test.ts; cross-reference docs/integrations/GITHUB.md and packages/github-bot/README.md.

Document the autofix ingress (autofix-ingress.ts → control-plane autofix queue): eligibility (reviews from the App + allowlisted bots), dedupe, and the rolling per-PR attempt limit enforced in control-plane autofix/service.ts and pr-autofix-feedback-store.

Explain session targeting: session-target.ts resolves the webhook repo, honoring repo-metadata defaultEnvironmentId; prompts.ts builds the review/comment prompts; responses post back through the GitHub App with proper permissions (Contents, Pull requests, Issues read/write).

Map the webhook pipeline in src/index.ts: signature verification (verify.ts), delivery dedupe via KV (processing/processed TTLs), payload schema parsing (payload-schemas.ts), then handlers.ts: PR opened (auto-review), review requested, issue/review comments (@mention).

pages.title: Linear Bot Integration
pages.purpose: The Linear bot worker: agent webhooks → session creation with team/project target mapping, model resolution, and progress/completion callbacks back to Linear.
instructions: Document the callback lifecycle: started/progress/completion activities posted back to Linear (callbacks.ts + callbacks/), HMAC-signed like the Slack path, with PR linkage to the resulting pull request.
Explain target resolution: team/project mappings select repositories or environments (target-resolution.ts, environments.ts) using shared repository/environment target contracts.

Note deployment via its own wrangler.toml and the trigger interplay with the control-plane automations (Linear trigger type is planned, not implemented); cross-reference docs/integrations/LINEAR.md and INTEGRATION.md.

Trace the Linear agent webhook (webhook-handler.ts): agent mention/assignment on issues creates a coding session; KV-backed state (kv-store.ts) tracks prompt/context; model resolution via model-resolution.ts.

pages.title: Model Provider Accounts
pages.purpose: Multi-provider model access: the shared model catalog, managed provider accounts (ChatGPT/SuperGrok OAuth device flows), credential storage, and per-session token brokering/refresh.
instructions: Managed accounts: model-provider-accounts/service.ts + device-authorization-service.ts run OAuth device flows for OpenAI and xAI (device-authorization-finalizer.ts), credentials stored encrypted (auth/provider-account-crypto.ts, db/model-provider-account-atomic-writer.ts, provider-account-credentials.ts), defaults + selection policy (selection-policy.ts, account-lifecycle-policy.ts).

Model catalog: shared/src/models.ts defines providers and VALID_MODELS (Anthropic, OpenAI/Codex via ChatGPT OAuth, xAI/SuperGrok, OpenCode Zen, Z.AI) with reasoning-effort config; deployment-wide enablement via db/model-preferences.ts and model-preferences routes.
Root provider-accounts.md is the long-form reference; docs/AVAILABLE_MODELS.md, OPENAI_MODELS.md, GROK_MODELS.md are the user-facing catalogs.

Runtime brokering: auth/model-provider-account-broker.ts + openai-token-broker.ts mint short-lived tokens to sandboxes; session/openai-token-refresh-service.ts and xai-token-refresh-service.ts refresh on session activity; per-session resolution via session/provider-account-resolution.ts; automations carry their own selections (automation-provider-selection.ts).

Sandbox side: sandbox-runtime plugins configure OpenCode for Codex/xAI OAuth (tests test_codex_auth_plugin_setup.py, test_xai_oauth_setup.py); managed OAuth refresh tokens are brokered by the control plane, never injected as env vars (docs/SECRETS.md).

pages.title: Slack Bot Integration
pages.purpose: The Slack bot worker: event/interaction routing, LLM target classification over repos and environments, session launch and prompt delivery, and completion callbacks.
instructions: Cover session interaction: session-launcher + prompt-delivery (including image attachments), per-user model/branch preferences (user-preferences.ts, app-home/), activity status updates (activity-status.ts), and completion/progress callbacks posting results back to threads (callbacks.ts).

Explain target resolution: the LLM classifier (classifier/index.ts over repos + environments via classifier/repos.ts and environments.ts), Slack routing rules and channel associations, the clarification picker when ambiguous (target-clarification.ts), and thread→session mapping (sessions/thread-session-store.ts).

Map the Hono worker: /webhooks/slack events + interactions routes (routes/events.ts, routes/interactions.ts), signature verification, dedupe, and signedControlPlaneFetch (internal-auth.ts) for all control-plane calls.
Note the App Home configuration surface, forwarded-message handling, and the Slack scopes required by slack-app-manifest.yaml; cross-reference docs/integrations/SLACK.md for user-facing behavior.

pages.title: Configuration & Secrets
pages.purpose: Configuration surface: env validation, secret scopes and injection into sandboxes, integration-settings resolution layers, sandbox settings, and SCM/model preferences.
instructions: Env validation: control-plane env-validation.ts requires token/repo-secrets encryption keys and validates required bindings; the rest of configuration arrives via Terraform vars (no wrangler.toml) or web .env.

Injection at spawn: session/user-env-resolver.ts merges user env + scoped secrets, sandbox/sandbox-env.ts builds the SessionConfig payload (repo manifest, base branches, tunnel settings, MCP servers) sent to the provider; managed OAuth tokens are brokered, not injected.

Integration settings layering: global defaults → per-repo overrides → environment overrides for sandbox and code-server (db/integration-settings.ts + session/integration-settings-resolution.ts); sandbox settings include tunnelPorts, child-session caps, timeouts (sandbox/settings.ts).
SCM settings (db/scm-settings.ts, routes/scm-settings.ts) and per-user model preferences round out the config surface.

Secret scopes and precedence (docs/SECRETS.md): global, repository, environment; a session receives global + its target's secrets — environment sessions do NOT inherit member-repo secrets, ad-hoc multi-repo sessions merge repo secrets with the primary repo winning collisions; .env paste import supported; AES-256-GCM at rest (db/scoped-secrets.ts, db/repo-secrets.ts, db/environment-secrets.ts, db/global-secrets.ts).

pages.title: Deployment & CI/CD
pages.purpose: How the system ships: Terraform layout and modules, D1 migrations, CI/CD workflows, Modal deployment, and the deployment gotchas that break deploys when ignored.
instructions: CI/CD: .github/workflows/ci.yml + ci-python.yml run lint/typecheck/tests per package on every push/PR; terraform.yml plans on PRs and applies on main (auto-deploy of workers, D1 migrations, web when web_platform=cloudflare); deploy-web.yml for Vercel; Modal data plane deploys from packages/modal-infra via deploy.py --build-sandbox-image (never deploy src/app.py directly; bump CACHE_BUSTER in images/base.py to force rebuilds).

Document the known gotchas from AGENTS.md/terraform README: two-phase deploys for new Durable Object bindings (enable_durable_object_bindings false then true), PKCS#8 GitHub App keys, Queues: Edit permission for image-build finalization, NEXT_PUBLIC_WS_URL needed at build time, and provider-account encryption key rotation rules.
Include secrets handling: wrangler-secrets.sh, Terraform tfvars vs GitHub secrets, and scripts/d1-migrate.sh for applying migrations; mention docs/GETTING_STARTED.md for the full deploy walkthrough.

Terraform: terraform/environments/production root modules split by concern (workers-*.tf, web-*.tf, d1.tf, modal.tf, daytona.tf, checks.tf, moved.tf) over reusable modules (cloudflare-worker with KV/DO/D1/Queue bindings, cloudflare-kv, vercel-project, modal-app CLI wrapper, daytona-infra); state in R2; control-plane wrangler config is Terraform-generated (no checked-in wrangler.toml).

pages.title: Observability & Debugging
pages.purpose: Structured logging, correlation IDs, and the debugging playbook for tracing one prompt across web, bots, control plane, sandbox infra, and the sandbox runtime.
instructions: Cover tooling: scripts/cf-logs.ts for querying Cloudflare logs, and the playbook's error-shape/joining recipes for debugging a prompt run across slack-bot → control-plane → modal-infra → sandbox.

Explain the common JSON log envelope (level, service, component, msg, ts) and the correlation fields (trace_id, request_id, session_id, message_id, sandbox_id, opencode_session_id) from docs/DEBUGGING_PLAYBOOK.md; snake_case at boundaries, camelCase only in local variables.

Point to the per-service loggers: control-plane/src/logger.ts (createLogger + CorrelationContext, session-scoped session-logger.ts), shared/src/logger.ts, sandbox-runtime log_config.py + boot_warnings.py (boot warnings file consumed by the bridge), slack/github/linear loggers.

Trace how correlation propagates: slack-bot generates trace_id → x-trace-id header → control-plane router into DO and provider calls → provider endpoints bind it into sandbox startup logs; web generates request ids at the /api edge and forwards only trace_id.

pages.title: Testing Strategy
pages.purpose: How the repo is tested and validated: Vitest unit vs workerd/D1 integration tests, Python pytest suites, test helpers and conventions, and repo-wide quality gates.
instructions: Integration-test hygiene: migrations applied via test/integration/apply-migrations.ts from terraform/d1/migrations; helpers.ts provides initSession/queryDO/seedEvents; shared D1 requires cleanD1Tables() in beforeEach/afterEach; config in vitest.integration.config.ts.

Layout conventions from AGENTS.md: TypeScript unit tests co-located as src/**/*.test.ts (web, slack-bot, linear-bot, control-plane); control-plane integration tests separately in test/integration running in workerd via @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers with real D1; github-bot tests in test/; Python tests as tests/test_*.py (modal-infra) and tests/ (sandbox-runtime, including the large bridge SSE suite).

Note behavioral specs embedded in unit tests worth consulting before changing behavior: message-queue.test.ts (prompt/stop semantics), sandbox/lifecycle/manager.test.ts (spawn decisions), pull-request-service tests (per-branch PR rules), automations routes/scheduler tests, spawn-children integration tests.
Prefer the narrowest quiet validation that proves the changed behavior; preserve complete failure output (AGENTS.md OpenWiki note).

Repo-wide quality gates: eslint (with scripts/lint-complexity.mjs complexity limits + reporter test), prettier, knip for unused exports, tsc typecheck, ruff for Python (ruff.toml), and lint-staged/husky pre-commit; run npm run build -w @open-inspect/shared before typecheck.

pages.title: Automations Flow
pages.purpose: Scheduled and event-driven automations: trigger registry and conditions, the D1-backed scheduler tick, invocations/runs, multi-repo fan-out, inbound webhooks, and completion callbacks.
instructions: Cover repository targeting: automation_repositories/automation_environments live selections (automation/repository.ts, automation/session-target.ts); scheduled automations fan out to up to 10 repos (one session per repo), event-driven triggers stay single-repo.

Detail the Scheduler (scheduler/scheduler.ts): tick = recovery sweep + overdue automations (MAX_PER_TICK 25, child-run launch cap), Trigger (manual), RunComplete (DO completion callback); invocation rows carry trigger_key dedupe + concurrency keys; status is derived from runs (DERIVED_INVOCATION_STATUS_SQL); auto-pause after 3 consecutive failures.

Document the inbound webhook routes (webhooks/automation-webhook.ts with one-time API key, webhooks/sentry.ts, webhooks/github.ts, webhooks/slack.ts) and completion callbacks to Slack (scheduler/slack-completion.ts) plus HMAC-signed bot callbacks (callback-notification-service.ts, callback-delivery.ts).

Explain the trigger registry in shared/src/triggers/ (schedule via shared/cron.ts, inbound webhook, Sentry alert, Slack message, GitHub events incl. Actions workflow runs) with condition matching (conditions.ts, glob.ts) and per-trigger validation.

Mention automation model-provider selections (model-provider-accounts/automation-provider-selection.ts) and the MIN_CRON_INTERVAL_MINUTES 15 rule from routes/automations.ts; embed a mermaid flowchart trigger → conditions → invocation → sessions → completion (mermaid-diagrams skill).

pages.title: Child Sessions
pages.purpose: Agent-spawned parallel child sessions: the sandbox tools, control-plane spawn route, depth/concurrency guardrails, and status/cancel coordination.
instructions: Cover coordination tools: send-child-prompt queues follow-ups into direct children, get-child-status (child-summary.handler.ts aggregates), cancel-child; child_activity.py tracks child state in the sandbox; session-with-children UI groups them in web.
Cross-reference integration tests (test/integration/spawn-children.test.ts, child-session-ops.test.ts) as behavioral spec for the guardrails.

Document the guardrails: MAX_SPAWN_DEPTH = 2, per-session concurrent and total child caps (DEFAULT_MAX_CONCURRENT_CHILD_SESSIONS / DEFAULT_MAX_TOTAL_CHILD_SESSIONS in shared integrations types), per-repo limits enforced by the child spawn route.

Trace the flow from the in-sandbox agent tools (sandbox-runtime/tools/spawn-child.js etc.) → DO internal routes (session/contracts.ts SessionInternalPaths) → routes/session-child-spawn.ts which creates a real child session via initializeSession with parentSessionId, spawnSource, spawnDepth.

pages.title: Git & Pull Requests
pages.purpose: Git operations end to end: SCM credential brokering for clones/pushes, the push command protocol, per-repo PR creation rules, PR lifecycle webhooks, and the autofix feedback loop.
instructions: Cover the PR lifecycle webhook (webhooks/pull-request-lifecycle.ts) and the autofix feedback loop (github-bot autofix-ingress → control-plane queue → autofix/service.ts → DO re-prompt) with its dedupe and per-PR attempt limits.

Git auth: in-sandbox git credential helper (sandbox-runtime credentials/git_credential_helper.py) → POST /sessions/:id/scm-credentials → scm-credentials-service.ts → provider token minting (GitHub App installation token for github, token for gitlab; providers must implement generateCredentialHelperAuth).
Include commit attribution (identity.ts, message_attribution.py) and optional SSH commit signing (routes/commit-signing.ts + git_signing.py).

PR creation: SessionPullRequestService per repository — multi-repo sessions open one PR per repo; one open PR per head branch; repeat calls force-push and reuse (updated: true); merged/closed PRs release the head branch (pull-request-refresh.ts + db/session-pull-request-store.ts); PRs are created with the prompting user's OAuth token when available, falling back to the shared GitHub App bot.

Push flow: SandboxPushService sends the push command over the sandbox socket and correlates the later push_complete/push_error event — the protocol's only request/response exchange (PUSH_TIMEOUT_MS); explain why the pending-resolver table lives in session-scoped state.

pages.title: Image Builds Pipeline
pages.purpose: Prebuilt-image pipeline for repos and environments: scheduling, build sandboxes, provider adapters, callback + queue finalization, reaping, and image selection at spawn.
instructions: Embed a mermaid flowchart of the build pipeline (mermaid-diagrams skill).

Explain selection at spawn: sandbox/lifecycle/image-selection.ts + image-builds/lookup.ts match fingerprint + runtime version; provider-policy.ts gates which providers support builds; concurrency.ts caps parallel builds.

Model the unified image_builds registry: scope kinds (repository and environment) with scope_id, per-repo SHAs (repository_shas), a repositories fingerprint for spawn matching, runtime version compatibility floor, and callback-token/queue-lease state (db/image-builds.ts, README D1 section).
Note the operational prerequisites: Cloudflare Queues: Edit permission, IMAGE_BUILD_SCHEDULER_CRON in index.ts, and that build-mode setup.sh failures are fatal (README repository lifecycle rules).

Trace the pipeline: image-builds/scheduler.ts cron → planner.ts + rebuild-policy.ts → provider-factory + adapters (modal-adapter, vercel-adapter, opencomputer-adapter) create a build sandbox and bind its provider session id → runtime boots in image-build mode (sandbox-runtime modal_image_build_start.py / entrypoint build mode; modal-infra sandbox/build_session.py) → success/failure callbacks (callback-auth.ts) → Cloudflare Queue finalization (finalization-consumer.ts, finalizer.ts, finalization-job.ts) with DLQ; reaper.ts and maintenance.ts clean stragglers.

pages.title: Managed Skills
pages.purpose: Reusable agent instructions: skill CRUD and git import with content addressing, assignment and revision pinning at session create, and materialization into the sandbox.
instructions: Authoring/import: routes/skills.ts CRUD + skills/git-import.ts importing skills from GitHub/GitLab repos with full file preview, pinned source revision, provenance, and validation (content-addressing.ts hashes content; skill-markdown.ts parses SKILL.md); skill_profiles.ts powers personal profiles.

Materialization: sandbox-runtime managed_skills.py fetches the pinned manifest from the control plane at boot (using the sandbox token) and writes skills into the OpenCode global config dir; bundled skills (agent-browser, record-video, upload-screenshot, visual-verification) ship in the runtime image.
Point to integration tests (test/integration/managed-skills.test.ts, sandbox-runtime tests/test_managed_skills.py) as the behavioral contract for pinning and materialization.
Resolution at session create: session/skill-resolution.ts selects global/repo/environment-assigned skills plus personal profiles and pins exact revisions onto the session (db/session-skills.ts).

pages.title: Media & Attachments
pages.purpose: Media handling: screenshots/videos as artifacts, prompt image attachments, R2 storage, limits and TTL pruning, and how Slack attachments become prompt attachments.
instructions: Document R2-backed media (storage/object-storage.ts, routes/responses/stored-object-response.ts) and the limits enforced in control-plane media.ts: screenshots 10MB / 100 per session, videos 100MB / 20 per session / 90s duration, prompt attachments 100 count and 500MB total per session, unreferenced attachments pruned after 24h (SESSION_ATTACHMENT_UNREFERENCED_TTL_MS).

Explain artifact metadata (session/artifact-metadata.ts, shared/types/artifacts.ts) and how screenshots/preview artifacts surface in the timeline; web rendering via media-lightbox and screenshot-artifact-card.
Note validation gates: mime type allowlists, per-session counters in DO SQLite, and the multipart size pre-check before formData buffering.

Trace upload paths: session-media-upload.ts / session-attachments.ts routes, the sandbox screenshot/video tools and attachment_processor.py hydration into prompts, and Slack file attachments (slack-bot/attachments.ts) forwarded as prompt attachments.

pages.title: Prompt Lifecycle
pages.purpose: The core loop: prompt enqueue → queue → sandbox delivery → OpenCode execution → event streaming back → persistence, broadcast, artifacts, and snapshot.
instructions: Cover artifact creation from events (artifact handlers, pr-artifacts.ts) and snapshot capture after successful completion (link to workflows/sandbox-lifecycle).
Document stop-execution semantics and queued-prompt draining (message-queue.ts), plus session-status-service transitions and title-service naming during runs.
Embed a mermaid sequenceDiagram (user → client → SessionDO → sandbox bridge → OpenCode → events → broadcast) per the mermaid-diagrams skill; avoid angle brackets and reserved words in labels.
Include the Slack/Linear tool-call progress callbacks (callback-notification-service.ts) that fire during the run.

Walk the flow end to end: prompt arrives (web socket or POST /sessions/:id/prompt) → enqueue-prompt-contract → SessionMessageQueue (ordering, MAX_UNFINISHED_PROMPTS queue cap, participant + git-identity attribution, attachment resolution) → prompt delivered over the sandbox WebSocket → bridge.py feeds OpenCode via prompt_stream.py → events stream back (event_forwarder.py) → session/sandbox-events/processor.ts classifies them (execution, streaming, artifact, runtime handlers) → event-repository persists → broadcast to all clients via websocket-manager.

pages.title: Sandbox Lifecycle
pages.purpose: The sandbox state machine: spawn/restore/warm decisions, inactivity and heartbeat timeouts, circuit breaker, snapshots vs persistent resume, and alarm-driven lifecycle.
instructions: Cover alarm-driven deadlines (session/alarm/handler.ts + scheduler.ts) and reconnect semantics: losing the sandbox WebSocket does NOT stop the sandbox; explicit lifecycle paths persist stopped/stale before closing to prevent reconnection (see components doc comment in HOW_IT_WORKS).

Document snapshot capture points (after successful prompt, before inactivity timeout, explicit) and the persistent-provider alternative: Daytona/E2B stop + resume the same sandbox; snapshot-capable providers restore state.
Embed a mermaid stateDiagram-v2 of the sandbox statuses and transitions (per the mermaid-diagrams skill).

Explain the three boot paths from HOW_IT_WORKS: fresh (clone → setup.sh → start.sh → agent ready), snapshot restore (restore → quick sync → start.sh), prebuilt image (incremental sync, setup skipped, start.sh strict); multi-repo runs steps 2–4 per repository in position order.

Map the sandbox row state machine using sandbox/sandbox-status.ts plus lifecycle/decisions.ts: spawn vs restore vs prebuilt-image start, warming, connecting timeout, inactivity timeout, stale heartbeat, circuit breaker (spawn_failure_count/last_spawn_failure), provider replacement stop.

pages.title: Session Creation Flow
pages.purpose: End-to-end session creation from every entry point (web, Slack, GitHub, Linear, automation, child spawn) through target resolution, initializeSession, and DO initialization.
instructions: Cover target resolution details: environment targeting (db/environments.ts), repo-id resolution (session/repo-id-resolution.ts), default-branch/branch resolution (repos/resolve.ts, repos/default-branch.ts), and provider account resolution at create time (session/provider-account-resolution.ts).
Embed a mermaid flowchart from entry points → create route → initializeSession → DO init → spawn (per the mermaid-diagrams skill).
Explain session-scoped settings folded in at create: sandbox settings, code-server/VNC flags, user env/secrets scoping, managed skills pinning (session/skill-resolution.ts).

Show that every client entry point converges here: web target picker (use-session-target-picker), slack-bot sessions/session-launcher.ts, github-bot session-target.ts, linear-bot target-resolution.ts, automation runs (scheduler → initializeSession), and child spawns (routes/session-child-spawn.ts with spawn-context.ts).

Trace POST /sessions (routes/session-create.ts) → create-session-input.ts validation → session/initialize.ts (SessionInitInput: repositories, environmentId, providerAuth snapshot, managed-skills manifest, lineage fields) → DO SessionInitHandler writing the session + repositories rows.

pages.title: Quickstart & Task Routing
pages.purpose: Entry point: orient a coding agent in the Open-Inspect monorepo, give the working commands (install, build order, lint, typecheck, tests), and route every common task to the right wiki page.
instructions: Core commands: npm install, npm run build / typecheck / lint:fix / format, npm test and npm run test:integration per workspace; Python packages use pytest (packages/modal-infra, packages/sandbox-runtime) and ruff for lint/format.

Describe the monorepo layout: npm workspaces packages/* plus Terraform at terraform/; build @open-inspect/shared FIRST before other TypeScript packages (npm run build -w @open-inspect/shared) because they import its built output.

Note that docs/ (HOW_IT_WORKS, GETTING_STARTED, AUTOMATIONS, SECRETS, MANAGED_SKILLS) is authoritative user documentation and packages/control-plane/README.md documents the API and WebSocket protocol; the wiki pages cross-reference rather than duplicate it.

Point to AGENTS.md for repo conventions (seconds in Python, milliseconds with _MS suffix in TypeScript, conventional commits, nested repo_owner rule) and CONTRIBUTING.md for process; mention docs/SETUP_GUIDE.md as the practical setup path.

Route readers through the hierarchy: architecture/ for how the system is built, concepts/ for domain vocabulary, workflows/ for end-to-end flows, integrations/ for the bot packages, operations/ for deployment/config/logging, testing/ for validation strategy. Give a one-line task-routing hint per group (e.g. 'changing sandbox spawn behavior → architecture/sandbox-providers + workflows/sandbox-lifecycle').
